one_way_hebrew: טהר and צרעת — the cleansing told in the vocabulary of Lev 13-14 (תורת המצורע... וטהר) and of Naaman (2 Kgs 5:14, ויטהר). Greek καθαρίζω translates the priestly verb; in Hebrew the scene walks straight into v. 4's command to keep the leper-torah.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (8:3): ובאותה] באותה DEF; אני] omit G.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to him: Take heed{H8104} lest{H6435} you tell{H5046} any man{H120}; but go{H1980} to the priest{H3548} to offer{H7126} your offerings{H7133}, as Moshe{H4872} commanded{H6680} in your Torah{H8451}.

one_way_hebrew: להקריב קרבניך — Leviticus' own cognate pair (הקריב קרבן, Lev 1:2): the healed man is sent directly into the leper-torah of Lev 14. The healer's first command after cleansing is Torah-obedience — the symbol-laden healing ends in the literal commandment, not instead of it.
greek_deviations: בתורתכם — 'in YOUR Torah': the possessive stands in no Greek text ('the gift that Moses commanded'). The suffix reads like a copyist's shaping in transmission; Howard renders 'as Moses commanded in your law.'

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when he entered{H935} Kfar{H3723} Nachum{H5151} ha-Martah, a captain{H8269} of hundreds{H3967} came{H935} to him and implored{H2603} him,

Howard's apparatus (8:5): המרתה] הרמתה AEF; כבואו] בבואו ACDG.

verses.translation: saying{H559}: My lord{H113}, my son{H1121} lies{H7901} in my house{H1004} with the sickness{H2483} of contraction — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, paralishiza — and he is convulsed{H2342} by the illness{H4245}.

one_way_hebrew: בני — 'MY SON lies in my house': Greek ὁ παῖς μου is ambiguous (boy or servant); the Hebrew is unambiguous, and v. 13 calls him הנער ('the lad'). John 4:46-53 tells the Capernaum officer's story of his SON — the Hebrew Matthew stands with John's construal.

חולי הכווץ glossed בלעז פירא״לשיזה — a native Hebrew medical phrase ('the sickness of contraction') glossed with the Romance word for paralysis; mss ACDEFG carry פרלאטיקו (paralitico). The gloss again runs Hebrew-to-foreign, as at 6:2 and 24:14.

ומתחלחל (H2342, hithpalpel) — Esther's convulsion: ותתחלחל המלכה מאד ('the queen was exceedingly convulsed,' Esth 4:4). Greek 'grievously tormented' (δεινῶς βασανιζόμενος) translates the sense, not the word.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (8:6): פיראלשיזה] פרלאטיקו ACDEFG, פיראלאשינו B, פיראלשיאה DG; בלעז] לעז A; הכווץ] הכיווץ G.

verses.translation: And the captain{H8269} of hundreds{H3967} answered{H6030} and said{H559} to him: My lord{H113}, it is not fitting that you come{H935} under{H8478} my roof{H1406}; only decree{H1504} a word{H562}, and he will be healed{H7495}.

one_way_hebrew: שתגזור אומר — Job 22:28's exact idiom: ותגזר אומר ויקם לך ('Thou shalt decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee'). Both rare words — גזר ('decree,' H1504) and אֹמֶר ('utterance,' H562) — stand together only there. The captain credits Yeshua with the restored man's Joban power: decree, and it stands. Greek 'only say the word' (μόνον εἰπὲ λόγῳ) cannot carry the allusion.
translation_notes: אינך ראוי — literally 'YOU are not fit to come under my roof,' i.e., my roof is unworthy of you; G reads איני ('I am not worthy'), and Howard renders '(I) am not worthy.' The base text puts the unworthiness on the house, not the guest's honor — the same humility from the other side.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (8:8): ויען] + אליו ABDEFG; אינך] איני G; לו] omit G.

Greek's 'outer darkness' locates; the Hebrew mourns. And the place bears its Hebrew name: Gehinnom.

verses.translation: And at evening{H6153} time{H6256} they brought{H935} to him those seized{H270} by the demons{H7700}, and he healed them{H7495} by his utterance{H3982} alone{H905}, and every sickness{H2483} he healed{H7495},

Avot 5:1). Healing by ma'amar alone places the act in creation's category; Greek λόγῳ says only 'with a word.'

verses.translation: to complete{H1584} what was said{H559} by Isaiah{H3470} the prophet{H5030}, of blessed memory: Surely{H403} our sicknesses{H2483} he bore{H5375}, and our pains{H4341} he carried{H5445}.

one_way_hebrew: The citation is Isa 53:4 in Isaiah's own consonants: אכן חלינו הוא נשא ומכאבינו סבלם. Greek Matthew's rendering of this verse famously matches neither the LXX nor the Hebrew exactly; the Shem Tov text simply writes Isaiah. And the narrative's own words are Isaiah's words — חלי (vv. 16-17) and מכאוב (cf. 24:8): the healings are told inside the Suffering-Servant vocabulary.
ז״ל — 'of blessed memory' (זכרונו לברכה) attached to Isaiah's name inside the running text: a Hebrew scribe's reflex, transmitted nowhere in Greek.
לגמור (H1584) — 'to COMPLETE': the psalmist's verb of God finishing what concerns him (Ps 57:3; 138:8), where Greek has πληρωθῇ ('be fulfilled'). The saying is brought to its full measure.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (8:17): חליינו] חילנו C; הנביא ז״ל] omit A; ע״י] על פי ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} him: The foxes{H7776} have holes{H2356} and the birds{H5775} have nests{H7064}, but the Son{H1121} of Man{H120}, the son of the virgin{H1330}, has no{H369} place{H4725} to bring in{H3664} his head{H7218}.

one_way_hebrew: שועלים... חורים — the foxes of Judg 15:4 and Song 2:15 in native idiom; חור (H2356) is the creature's hole of Nah 2:13. The homeless Son of Man is measured against Scripture's animal homes, word by word.

The phrase stands in no Greek manuscript of Matthew; it is the Shem Tov text's own epithet, reading בן אדם through Isa 7:14's sign-child. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew lacks it ('the Son of man does not have a place where he can bow down his head') — the reading belongs to the Shem Tov family. Howard: 'the Son of Man, the son of the virgin, has no place to enter his head.'

verses.translation: And there was a great{H1419} tempest{H5591} in the sea{H3220}, and the waves{H1530} were coming on{H1980} exceedingly{H3966}, and the ship{H591} was about{H2803} to be broken up{H7665}.

one_way_hebrew: The verse is built of Jonah 1:4's own words: ויהי סער גדול בים... והאניה חשבה להשבר ('there was a mighty tempest in the sea, and the ship was like to be broken'). The rare personification חשבה להשבר — the ship 'thinking' to break — occurs in Scripture only in Jonah, and the Hebrew Matthew reuses it verbatim. Greek Matthew has σεισμὸς μέγας ('a great shaking') and no thinking ship. The storm is written as a sign-of-Jonah scene — sleeping master, terrified cry, stilled sea (vv. 25-26) follow Jonah's sequence.
greek_deviations: No sleeping: Greek 8:24 ends 'but he was asleep' (αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκάθευδεν); the Shem Tov base text never says it — see v. 25.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (8:24): הולכים מאד] נכנסים באניה ABDEFG ('coming into the ship,' as Mark 4:37); בים] omit EF; והאניה] והוא G.

verses.translation: And his disciples{H8527} approached{H7126} him and besought{H1245} him, saying{H559}: Our lord{H113}, save us{H3467}, lest{H6435} we perish{H6}!

one_way_hebrew: הושיענו פן נאבד — Jonah 1:6's plea ('call upon thy God... that we perish not,' ולא נאבד) spoken with the salvation-verb ישע, the root of the name ישו״ע: the cry to the master of the storm carries the Savior's own name. Greek 'Lord, save us, we perish' translates the words; only the Hebrew sounds the name.
greek_deviations: No waking: mss ABDEFG read ויקיצוהו ('and they woke him'), as in the Greek; in the base text the disciples simply approach and beseech — the text never said he slept (v. 24 note).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (8:25): ויבקשו ממנו] ויקיצוהו ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Why do you look at one another{H7200}, O you of little{H6996} faith{H548}? And he arose{H6965} and commanded{H6680} the sea{H3220} and the winds{H7307} to rest{H5117}, and immediately they rested{H5117}.
words: do you look at one another

one_way_hebrew: למה תתראו — 'Why do you look at one another?': Jacob's words to his sons in the famine, Gen 42:1 — the one biblical occurrence of this hithpael — men trading helpless glances instead of acting on trust. The base text quotes Genesis; Greek τί δειλοί ἐστε ('why are you fearful') matches the variants (תראו ABDEFG), not the base.
מקטני אמנה — again the full rabbinic idiom (b. Sotah 48b; see 6:30), with the same מ the base ms used there: the ms is consistent where the Greek has only ὀλιγόπιστοι.

שינוחו... נחו — the sea commanded to REST (נוח): 'He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still' (Ps 107:29); 'and the sea ceased from her raging' (Jonah 1:15). The Jonah-sequence completes.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (8:26): תתראו] תראו ABDEFG; מקטני] קטני ABDEFG; אליהם] להם A; ויקם] omit A.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 8 in the Shem Tov Hebrew carries readings found in no Greek manuscript and tells its miracles in Scripture's own sentences. (1) 8:20 reads 'the Son of Man, THE SON OF THE VIRGIN (בן הבתולה), has no place to bring in his head' — a Shem Tov-family epithet absent from every Greek ms and from the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew. (2) 8:24 is built of Jonah 1:4 verbatim — סער גדול בים... והאניה חשבה להשבר ('the ship thought to break up,' Jonah's unique personification) — and 8:25 cries Jonah 1:6's cry with the verb of Yeshua's own name (הושיענו פן נאבד); the base text has no sleeping and no waking (mss add ויקיצוהו). The storm is written as a sign-of-Jonah scene. (3) 8:26 asks Gen 42:1's exact question, 'Why do you look at one another (למה תתראו)?', and repeats the rabbinic מקטני אמנה (b. Sotah 48b; cf. 6:30). (4) 8:8-9: the captain speaks Job 22:28 — 'decree a word (שתגזור אומר) and he will be healed' — and confesses 'I am a SINFUL man' where Greek has 'a man under authority'; his sick one is 'my SON' (v. 6), 'the lad' (v. 13), with John 4:46-53. (5) 8:17 quotes Isa 53:4 in Isaiah's own consonants, adding ז״ל ('of blessed memory') to Isaiah's name — a Jewish scribal honorific no Greek transmits. (6) 8:11-12: the many from east and west will REST (וינוחו) with Abraham, and the sons of the kingdom go to 'the DARK PLACES (מחשכי, Ps 88:7) of GEHINNOM' (base יש לנו is corrupt for ישלכו 'will be cast'; 'clenching' ותחזק for B's 'gnashing'). (7) 8:16 heals 'by his UTTERANCE (מאמר) alone' — the rabbis' creation-word (m. Avot 5:1); 8:29 expels the demons as 'EVIL CAMPS (מחנות רעות),' a command absent from the Greek. (8) The annotating habit continues: paralishiza glosses 'the sickness of contraction' (8:6), Ginitraros glosses 'the realm of the Gargizani' (8:28, base Gergesene where mss read Gadarene); Kfar Nachum bears the surname ha-Martah (8:5). (9) 8:33-34 close in Ruth 1:19's idiom (ותהום כל העיר) and Moses' — inverted — intercession idiom (ויחלו פניו, Exod 32:11). (10) 8:10 base reads starkly 'I have not found great faith in Israel' (mss soften with 'like this'). Scan corrections to the transcription: 8:13's final sentence restored (ונרפא הנער בעת ההיא); 8:19 בכל; 8:20 יש״ו; 8:28 במלכות, ויפגעו; 8:30 מהם; 8:31 ויפגעו; abbreviation marks set right (אדו׳, לא״, א״, וא׳). Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 5 (Perek 32), 14 (33), 18 (34), 23 (35), and 28 (36).
